class.name: ResourceTextSerializer
class.brief_description: Converts any [Resource] to JSON, INI, CSV, XML or TOML text and back, based on its stored properties.
class.description: [ResourceTextSerializer] maps the properties of a [Resource] that have [constant @GlobalScope.PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE] to text that players and other tools can read and edit. The same mapping is used by [ResourceSaver] and [ResourceLoader] for the file extensions [code].json[/code], [code].ini[/code], [code].csv[/code] and [code].xml[/code] (and [code].toml[/code] with the TOML module), so in most cases a call to [method ResourceSaver.save] and [method ResourceLoader.load] is all that is needed. [method serialize] and [method deserialize] do the same with strings, for example to send a resource over the network or to store it in a database. The format is given by name; [method get_formats] lists the available ones. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var settings = AudioBusSettings.new() # A Resource with class_name AudioBusSettings. settings.master_volume = 0.8 ResourceSaver.save(settings, "user://audio.json") ResourceSaver.save(settings, "user://audio.xml") var loaded = ResourceLoader.load("user://audio.json") as AudioBusSettings print(loaded.master_volume) # Prints 0.8 # The same as text, without a file: var text = ResourceTextSerializer.serialize(settings, &"xml") var copy = ResourceTextSerializer.deserialize(text, &"xml") as AudioBusSettings print(ResourceTextSerializer.get_formats()) # Prints ["json", "ini", "csv", "xml", "toml"] [/gdscript] [csharp] var settings = new AudioBusSettings(); // A [GlobalClass] Resource. settings.MasterVolume = 0.8f; ResourceSaver.Save(settings, "user://audio.json"); ResourceSaver.Save(settings, "user://audio.xml"); var loaded = ResourceLoader.Load("user://audio.json"); GD.Print(loaded.MasterVolume); // Prints 0.8 // The same as text, without a file: string text = ResourceTextSerializer.Serialize(settings, "xml"); var copy = (AudioBusSettings)ResourceTextSerializer.Deserialize(text, "xml"); GD.Print(string.Join(", ", ResourceTextSerializer.GetFormats())); // Prints json, ini, csv, xml, toml [/csharp] [/codeblocks] [b]JSON[/b] ([code]"json"[/code]): one object per resource. The root object has the keys [code]"$type"[/code] (the class name, for example [code]"AudioBusSettings"[/code]) and [code]"$format_version"[/code] (see [constant FORMAT_VERSION]), followed by one key per property in property order. Nested resources are nested objects, arrays of resources are arrays of objects. A nested object only has a [code]"$type"[/code] key if its class differs from the declared type of the property. A [code].json[/code] file without a [code]"$type"[/code] key that names a [Resource] class is still loaded as [JSON], as before; [method ResourceLoader.load] with a type hint (for example [code]load(path, "AudioBusSettings")[/code]) also reads such files as that type. [b]INI[/b] ([code]"ini"[/code]): one section per resource. The root resource is in [code][root][/code] with the key [code]$type[/code]; a nested resource is in its own section named after its path, for example [code][root/entries/0][/code]. By default the values use the Variant syntax of [ConfigFile] ([code]name="Ann"[/code], [code]size=Vector2(1, 2)[/code]). With [member ProjectSettings.filesystem/resources/text_formats/ini_plain_values] or the option [code]"plain"[/code], values are written without type syntax ([code]name=Ann[/code], [code]size=1, 2[/code], [code]color=#ff0000ff[/code]), so other tools can read them. Both styles are read. [b]CSV[/b] ([code]"csv"[/code]): only for list resources: a resource with exactly one typed array of resources (for example [code]Array[Entry][/code]) whose elements have only simple properties (no resources, arrays or dictionaries). The file has a header row with the property names and one row per element. A CSV file contains no type, so it must be loaded with a type hint: [code]ResourceLoader.load("user://voices.csv", "VoiceList")[/code] or [code]deserialize(text, &"csv", "VoiceList")[/code]. A resource that does not fit gives an error and no file is written; check it first with [method can_save_as_csv]. [b]XML[/b] ([code]"xml"[/code]): the root element [code][/code] has one child element per property, in property order: [code]0.8[/code]. Integers, floats, booleans and strings are text; a float always has a [code].[/code] ([code]1.0[/code]). Nested resources and dictionaries are elements with one child element per key; a key that is not a valid XML name is written as [code][/code]. Arrays have [code]kind="array"[/code]: arrays of numbers (vectors, packed arrays) as one text ([code]0.5, -2.0[/code]), other arrays with one [code][/code] per element. [code]kind="string"[/code] marks a string that would otherwise be read as a number or boolean ([code]007[/code]), [code]kind="null"[/code] marks [code]null[/code], [code]kind="dictionary"[/code] an empty dictionary. A nested resource has a [code]type[/code] attribute only if its class differs from the declared type. Comments and CDATA sections are allowed when editing by hand. A [code].xml[/code] file is only loaded as a resource if its root element is [code][/code] with a [code]type[/code] attribute that names a [Resource] class; other XML files are left to other loaders. [b]Values:[/b] [Color] is written as [code]"#rrggbbaa"[/code] when that is exact, otherwise as an array of floats; vectors, rectangles and matrices as arrays of numbers; enums as their names (see [member ProjectSettings.filesystem/resources/text_formats/enums_as_names]); [StringName] and [NodePath] as strings. A resource that is saved in its own file is written as its path and loaded from that path. When loading, a key that is missing keeps the default value of the class, and an unknown key is skipped with a warning. Values are converted to the type of the property, so a hand-edited [code]"0.5"[/code] or [code]"yes"[/code] is accepted for a [float] or [bool] property. [b]Options[/b] of [method serialize] (options that are not given come from the project settings under [code]filesystem/resources/text_formats/[/code]): - [code]"indent"[/code] ([String]): indentation of JSON and XML; an empty string writes one line. - [code]"enums_as_names"[/code] ([bool]): enum properties as names or as numbers (all formats). - [code]"plain"[/code] ([bool]): INI values without type syntax. - [code]"delimiter"[/code] ([String], one character): CSV delimiter; also read by [method deserialize]. - [code]"defaults"[/code] ([Resource]): JSON and INI: values of the root resource that are equal to the same property of [code]"defaults"[/code] are not written (metadata is always written). Nested resources are written completely. [b]Note:[/b] JSON has only one number type. Integers above 2^53 lose precision, and properties of type [Variant] get [float] values back where [int] values were saved. In plain INI and in CSV, properties of type [Variant] come back as [String]. XML and TOML keep [int], [float], [bool] and [String] apart. [b]Note:[/b] [code].csv[/code] files in [code]res://[/code] are imported as translations by the editor. Keep CSV resources in [code]user://[/code], or set their importer to "Keep File" in the Import dock. [b]Note:[/b] The methods of this class can be called from any thread.

method.name: can_save_as_csv
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param resource] fits the CSV format: exactly one typed array of resources, elements of that type with only simple properties, and no other property that differs from its default value.

method.name: deserialize
method.description: Creates a resource from [param text] in the text format [param format] (see [method get_formats]). The class comes from the type stored in the text ([code]"$type"[/code] in JSON and TOML, [code]$type[/code] in the INI section [code][root][/code], the [code]type[/code] attribute of the XML root element), or from [param type_hint]. CSV text has no type, so [param type_hint] is required there. Option: [code]"delimiter"[/code] for CSV. Returns [code]null[/code] and prints an error if the text can't be read or the format is unknown. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var list = ResourceTextSerializer.deserialize(csv_text, &"csv", "VoiceList", { "delimiter": ";" }) [/gdscript] [csharp] var list = ResourceTextSerializer.Deserialize(csvText, "csv", "VoiceList", new Godot.Collections.Dictionary { { "delimiter", ";" } }); [/csharp] [/codeblocks]

method.name: dictionary_to_resource
method.description: Creates a resource from [param data], a [Dictionary] in the layout of [method resource_to_dictionary]. If [param data] has no [code]"$type"[/code] key, [param type_hint] gives the class. Returns [code]null[/code] and prints an error if no resource can be created.

method.name: get_formats
method.description: Returns the names of the text formats that [method serialize] and [method deserialize] accept, in the order they were registered: [code]"json"[/code], [code]"ini"[/code], [code]"csv"[/code] and [code]"xml"[/code] from the engine core, followed by formats of modules ([code]"toml"[/code] if the TOML module is part of the build).

method.name: has_format
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param format] is a registered text format (see [method get_formats]). Case and a leading dot are ignored, so [code]".JSON"[/code] is the same as [code]"json"[/code].

method.name: resource_to_dictionary
method.description: Returns [param resource] as a [Dictionary] that contains only JSON types ([Dictionary], [Array], [String], numbers, booleans and [code]null[/code]): the same layout as the JSON format. Options: [code]"enums_as_names"[/code] ([bool]) and [code]"defaults"[/code] ([Resource]): values of the root resource that are equal to the same property of [code]"defaults"[/code] are not written (metadata is always written).

method.name: serialize

constants.constant: Version of the text layout. It is written as [code]"$format_version"[/code] into JSON and TOML files, into the INI section [code][root][/code] and as the attribute [code]format_version[/code] of the XML root element. A file with a higher version is read with a warning.
